name: run the settlement and gluing the math already proves
asks: Finding from the 2026-07-16 briefing session on unwoven/unsettled math: exactly one Obsmetrologia result is realized against live firm data — reading-coordination-cost, a READOUT of the obstruction (rank Ȟ¹) — while the three operations the corpus proves as the work itself are never run over live pools: (1) SETTLEMENT, iterating the closure-rule system cl^S = lfp(T_S) (Obsmetrologia/Closure/RuleSystem.lean, the Datalog immediate-consequence operator) over accumulated evidence until quiescent; (2) GLUING/WEAVING, actually merging agreeing local sections into a global section (CRDT delta merge, Charge.joinList_congr; Ȟ¹=0 iff the family glues, SettlingCohomologyH1.lean); (3) ATTENTION ALLOCATION, the bounded-budget knapsack choosing which held-⊤ obstructions to reconcile (Cohomology/AttentionAllocation.lean). Today's live readout is Ȟ¹=0 with 107 vertices, 76 edges, 31 components — but this is vacuous gluing over a starved nerve: the movement data (prompts, replies, token costs, tool acts) never becomes records, so no edges exist to obstruct, and the offices whose lanes that data feeds sit as isolated vertices (chief-financial-officer, white/black/blue army, chairperson). Per agential-relationality: history has no settled sub-stream; settlement happens in the fibers above the history — and the firm keeps no history of its own movements. MetroPlat holds the capture formula already implemented as prior art (token-usage exact microdollar accounting, claude-session transcript reading, chronicle goals/obligations extraction, tool acts as four-valued charged claims, glueClaimSessions with the H¹ adjudication readout, plate:log with rebuild(t)=t) — to be re-realized as standalone enterprise instruments per the MetroPlat boundary, not hired as runtime. The labor division falls out of the math: deterministic settlement/gluing/readouts are scripts; bounded extraction and drafting under a validate-and-repair loop is free-endpoint work (drafting-a-term is the precedent); only judgment, dispatch, and verdict need Claude.
